name: Report verified workplace drug and alcohol test results to employers
sector: health care: workplace drug and alcohol testing
summary: Once a workplace drug or alcohol test has a final result, the company tells the employer's designated representative and queues the test for billing. Negatives from the laboratory get a short review against the donor's custody form by an MRO assistant before they are posted to the employer's secure web report or sent by secure fax; results verified by the medical review officer get a written report within two days; breath alcohol results are recorded for the employer's reports. Coordinators answer employer questions, fix billing exceptions and prepare statistical reports. Confidentiality rules limit who may receive a result, and missing custody form copies, stale fax numbers and wrong donor details cause most delays and corrections.

baseline.org_archetype: The workplace testing line of a large Canadian laboratory company reporting about 25,000 test results a month to more than 500 employers through a web report and secure fax.
baseline.notes: Procedures follow US DOT 49 CFR Part 40, by law for DOT-regulated donors and by contract for the rest.

trigger: A final result is ready to report: a certified laboratory negative, an MRO-verified result or a breath alcohol result.
end_state: The result is in the employer's web report or delivered by secure fax, counted in the employer's statistical reports, and the test is queued for billing.

volume.seasonality: Follows test volume, higher in spring and summer, with Monday and Tuesday peaks.

evidence.note: More than 300,000 drug tests a year is about 25,000 a month.

The company's MRO assistants review and enter negative results against custody forms and report results to company contacts following client preferences (dyn_mroa); staff review of negatives is allowed under the MRO's supervision (cfr40127). The role is not in the organisation file, which folds it into the program coordinator. Wage assumed near the Job Bank 13112 median times 1.35. FTE close to what hands-on time times volume implies.

Coordinators answer employer queries, fix billing exceptions and prepare activity and statistical reports and scorecards (dyn_dtsol). FTE: about 3 of the 18 coordinators, close to what hands-on time implies. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

The operations manager reviews monthly client scorecards and handles misdirected result reports; share of the two managers estimated. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Medical review officer (contracted physician, part time)

evidence.note: The MRO personally reviews a quality sample of staff-reviewed negatives (at least 5 percent, capped at 500 a quarter) and cancels the few with uncorrected flaws; FTE estimated from that sample. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Drug testing case management (chain of custody, MRO review, employer web reports)
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
Laboratory billing and accounts receivable system (provincial claims, patient, client invoices)

steps.name: Receive the result for reporting
steps.description: The drug testing case system receives a result that is ready to report: a certified negative from the laboratory, a result verified by the medical review officer, or a breath alcohol result keyed by the collector, and routes it to the right review queue.

evidence.note: Shares estimated from the about 7 percent of drug tests that go to medical review and the alcohol tests ordered alone; the organisation file sends all three result types to this process.

steps.name: Review the negative against custody form Copy 2
steps.description: An MRO assistant opens the negative with the Copy 2 image and checks that donor and specimen IDs match, the donor signed, the collector's entries are complete and the reason for test is recorded, then stamps the negative as reviewed for the MRO. Most negatives take well under a minute when the images match.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.127: Copy 2 review by the MRO or supervised staff before a negative is released to the employer. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

next.condition: Copy 2 missing or a correctable flaw
picked for the MRO's quality sample

evidence.note: Staff review of negatives against custody forms (cfr40127, dyn_mroa). Share with problems estimated.

steps.name: Ask the site for Copy 2 or a corrective statement
steps.description: The assistant faxes or emails the collection site for the missing Copy 2 or the collector's signed statement correcting the flaw, and holds the negative until it arrives.

evidence.note: Obtaining corrective documentation (dyn_mroa).

steps.name: Wait for the site's reply
steps.description: The company centre or third-party clinic faxes the copy or the signed statement, usually within a day or two; some flaws are never corrected.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Cancel the test for an uncorrected flaw
steps.description: The MRO reviews the uncorrected flaw, marks the test cancelled with the reason, and notes that the employer needs a new test where a negative result is required, such as pre-employment.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.127: only the MRO can cancel a test. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

steps.name: Report a negative-dilute that needs an observed recollection
steps.description: For a negative-dilute with creatinine between 2 and 5 mg/dL, the assistant, on the MRO's instruction, phones the DER that an immediate recollection under direct observation is required with minimal notice to the donor, and documents the call.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.197: MRO directs an immediate observed recollection for creatinine 2 to 5 mg/dL. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

evidence.note: Share of very dilute negatives estimated.

steps.name: Review the MRO's quality sample of negatives
steps.description: The MRO personally reviews a sample of the negatives the assistants have reviewed, plus every one that needed corrective action, to check the staff's work; the sample is capped at 500 negatives a quarter.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.127: MRO reviews at least 5 percent of staff-reviewed results each quarter, up to 500 negatives. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

evidence.note: 500 a quarter is about 167 of roughly 21,500 negatives a month, under 1 percent.

steps.name: Record the breath alcohol result
steps.description: A program coordinator checks the alcohol testing form image and the collector's keyed result. Results of 0.02 or more have already been phoned to the DER by the breath alcohol technician; for DOT donors the technician also sends the form directly, so the company only records the result for the employer's reports.

error.defect_description: Result recorded against the wrong donor.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.255: the technician reports 0.02 or more to the DER immediately and directly, not through service agents. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

steps.name: Prepare the written report of the MRO-verified result
steps.description: For a verified positive, refusal, verified negative or cancellation, the assistant checks that the MRO's phone report to the DER is documented where one was needed, attaches the signed Copy 2 image or MRO letter, and readies the written report so it reaches the DER within two days of verification.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.163 and 40.167: written report on Copy 2 or a letter, delivered within two days of verification, no quantitative values. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

steps.name: Check the account's reporting rules and recipients
steps.description: Before a non-negative report goes out, the assistant checks the program profile for who may receive it (the DER, a separate contact for applicants, or a third-party administrator acting for the employer), the delivery method and the secure fax number on file.

error.defect_description: Out-of-date recipient or fax number used.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.321 and 40.345 (results only to the employer's designated recipients or an intermediary the employer chose) and PIPEDA safeguards for health information. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

evidence.note: Client reporting preferences (dyn_mroa).

steps.name: Release the result to the employer
steps.description: The case system posts the result to the employer's secure web report and emails the DER a notice to log in, or sends it by secure fax for accounts that prefer fax, and updates the daily activity report.

next.condition: the DER or donor calls about the result

evidence.note: Web-based and secure fax reporting; activity reports of specimens received in the previous 24 hours (dyn_dtsol). Query share estimated.

steps.name: Resolve a failed fax delivery
steps.description: A coordinator checks the fax error, phones the DER to confirm the secure fax number or switch the account to web reporting, and resends the report.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Answer the employer's or donor's question about a result
steps.description: A coordinator takes the call or email, confirms the caller is a designated contact or the donor, and explains the status or the meaning of a result (for example a dilute negative), sends a copy, or takes a donor's written request for their own result. Errors in donor details or account found here are sent for correction.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.321: no release of individual results to third parties without specific written consent; identity checked before discussing a result. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

next.condition: donor details, reason or account wrong on the report
report went to someone not entitled to it

evidence.note: Assistants and coordinators answer customer and donor questions about results (dyn_mroa). Shares estimated.

steps.name: Correct and reissue the report
steps.description: The assistant corrects the donor's name or ID, the reason for test or the employer division, gets the MRO's approval where the MRO report itself changes, and reissues a corrected report marked as amended.

evidence.note: Only the MRO may change an MRO report (cfr40167).

steps.name: Handle a result sent to the wrong recipient
steps.description: The operations manager asks the wrong recipient to destroy or return the report, records the incident for the privacy office's assessment of real risk of significant harm, informs the employer, fixes the cause (often a stale fax number or contact) and has the report sent to the right contact.

control.basis: PIPEDA breach of security safeguards provisions: assess real risk of significant harm, report and notify where it exists, and keep a record of every breach for two years

evidence.note: Breach duties (opc_breach). Frequency and time estimated.

steps.name: Create the billable order
steps.description: The case system builds the billable order for the test from the account's price list: panel and laboratory fee, company or third-party collection fee, MRO review fee, alcohol test, after-hours callout or cancellation charge, and the employer's purchase order or cost centre.

next.condition: missing purchase order, unknown clinic fee or wrong division

evidence.note: Single laboratory and billing platform across Canada (dyn_dtsol). Exception share estimated.

steps.name: Resolve the billing exception
steps.description: A coordinator works the daily exception list: gets the purchase order or cost centre from the employer, adds the third-party clinic's fee from its invoice, or moves the charge to the right division.

error.defect_description: Charge moved to the wrong division.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Include the test in the employer's periodic reports
steps.description: The test is counted in the employer's statistical reports (by reason, result and location) and, for DOT employers, in the annual MIS data; a coordinator builds the custom monthly reports some employers ask for in a spreadsheet. The per-test time is the coordinator's monthly report work shared across the tests.

control.basis: 49 CFR 40.26: DOT employers report annual MIS data on the DOT form; the provider supplies the counts. For DOT-regulated donors this is fixed by law; for other Canadian donors it is adopted through the Canadian Model and employer contracts.

evidence.note: DOT-compliant and non-regulated statistical reports (dyn_dts, dyn_dtsol). Amortised time estimated.

steps.name: Review the client's monthly scorecard
steps.description: The operations manager reviews each large client's monthly scorecard (turnaround, cancellations, positivity, collection site performance) before it is sent and follows up on outliers. The per-test time is the review time shared across the client's tests.

evidence.note: Performance scorecards are offered (dyn_dts); review time estimated.

steps.name: Send the billable order to the billing system
steps.description: The nightly interface sends the day's billable orders to the billing and receivables system, where they wait for the employer's monthly invoice run.
outputs: billable order in the billing system

evidence.note: Nightly interface assumed.

exceptions.name: Missing Copy 2 or correctable flaw on a negative
exceptions.description: The negative is held until the site sends Copy 2 or a corrective statement; a few are cancelled by the MRO.

exceptions.name: Negative-dilute needing observed recollection
exceptions.description: The DER is told an immediate observed recollection is required.

exceptions.name: Employer or donor query
exceptions.description: The DER asks for status, a copy or an explanation, or the donor asks for their own result.

exceptions.name: Amended report
exceptions.description: Wrong donor details, reason or division are corrected and the report reissued.

exceptions.name: Result sent to the wrong recipient
exceptions.description: A report reaches someone not entitled to it; the incident is logged for breach assessment and the report resent.

exceptions.name: Billing exception
exceptions.description: A missing purchase order, unknown clinic fee or wrong division holds the billable order.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from final result available to result delivered and billable order sent to billing
benchmarks.population: Workplace drug and alcohol test results at a Canadian testing provider

evidence.note: No opened source gives this interval. The company releases negatives within 6 to 24 hours of laboratory receipt (dyn_dtsol), which leaves hours for this review, written MRO reports are due within two days (cfr40167), and the billable order waits for a nightly interface.

benchmarks.unit: share of staff-reviewed results and maximum negatives per quarter

benchmarks.population: MRO records of DOT drug tests

pain_points.description: Negatives cannot be released until Copy 2 is on file, and third-party clinics often send it late or with errors.
Every negative is looked at by a person even when the images match, which takes most of the MRO assistants' reporting time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the touch times.

pain_points.description: Secure fax delivery depends on fax numbers kept current by employers; stale numbers cause failed sends and misdirected reports that are privacy breaches.
Employers phone for status and copies that are already in the web report, taking coordinator time.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Billing needs purchase orders and clinic fees that are often missing at the time of the test.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Drug testing services
sources.supports: More than 300,000 drug tests a year; more than 70 company centres and more than 2,000 preferred third-party collection sites; negatives usually released within 24 hours and non-negatives need another 48 to 72 hours; web-based and secure fax result reporting; DOT-compliant and non-regulated statistical reports; performance scorecards; post-accident, random and other testing reasons.

sources.title: Drug testing solutions
sources.supports: Negatives generally released within 6 to 24 hours, non-negatives another 48 to 72 hours; web-based and secure fax reporting; activity reports of specimens received in the previous 24 hours with status and result; DOT-compliant and non-regulated statistical reports; performance scorecards; single laboratory and billing platform; scientific consultants; inquiries to a drug testing mailbox.

sources.title: Medical review officer assistant (job posting)
sources.supports: MRO assistants review and enter negative and non-negative laboratory results against custody and control forms, assist the MRO including arranging split specimen tests and contacting the DER to arrange an interview between the MRO and a donor, track turnaround and escalate delays, review documentation for fatal or correctable errors and obtain corrective documentation, report results to company contacts following client reporting preferences, and answer donor and customer calls; follows DOT rules and the Canadian Model; high school diploma; Monday to Friday plus on-call rotation.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.127 MRO functions in reviewing negative test results
sources.supports: MRO or staff under direct supervision review CCF Copy 2 for fatal or correctable errors and match it to the negative laboratory result before release; the MRO personally reviews at least 5 percent of staff-reviewed results each quarter, including all needing corrective action, but need not review more than 500 negatives a quarter.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.163 How does the MRO report drug test results?
sources.supports: The MRO reports all results to the employer on a signed copy of Copy 2 or a written report with name, specimen ID, reason, dates, result and drug; only negatives may be reported as electronic data files; quantitative values are not given to employers; negative and cancelled records kept one year, positives and refusals five years.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.167 How are MRO reports of drug results transmitted to the employer?
sources.supports: Verified positives, refusals and results needing immediate observed recollection must reach the DER the same day as verification or the next business day, preferably by telephone followed by documentation; written reports must reach the DER within two days of verification by fax, courier, mail or electronic image; transmissions must be secure.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.197 What happens when an employer receives a report of a dilute specimen?
sources.supports: A negative-dilute result with creatinine of 2 to 5 mg/dL requires an immediate recollection under direct observation directed by the MRO; above 5 mg/dL the employer may order an unobserved retest; minimum advance notice; declining is a refusal.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.255 What are the requirements for BATs and STTs to report alcohol test results?
sources.supports: The breath alcohol technician immediately notifies the DER of any result of 0.02 or greater by telephone, secure fax or other immediate means, follows non-written reports with Copy 1 of the alcohol testing form, transmits confidentially and not through C/TPAs or other service agents.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.321 What is the general confidentiality rule for drug and alcohol test information?
sources.supports: Service agents and employers may not release individual test results or medical information to third parties without the employee's specific written consent naming the information, recipient and time.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.345 In what circumstances may a C/TPA act as an intermediary in the transmission of drug and alcohol testing information to employers?
sources.supports: A C/TPA may pass MRO results to the DER only where the employer chooses and must meet the MRO's confidentiality and timing requirements in 40.167.

sources.title: 49 CFR 40.26 What form must an employer use to report Management Information System (MIS) data to a DOT agency?
sources.supports: Employers report MIS data on the DOT Drug and Alcohol Testing MIS Data Collection Form following the submission rules of their DOT agency.

sources.title: What you need to know about mandatory reporting of breaches of security safeguards
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Breaches posing a real risk of significant harm must be reported to the OPC and affected individuals notified as soon as feasible; health information is usually sensitive; records of every breach kept two years.

sources.title: Wages: Medical administrative assistant in Ontario (NOC 13112)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 25.00, high 32.70 CAD (2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one reported test. A drug and alcohol test done together is one report.

The toxicology workflow describes the laboratory sending negatives to the MRO queue and the employer report in one system step; here the employer posting happens after the MRO staff review of Copy 2, as the rules require. The two together stay within the company's 6 to 24 hours for negatives.
The MRO assistant role is not in the organisation file and is added because the company posts it as a separate job and the coordinators are largely used by test ordering. Its cost is an estimate.

Monthly statistical reports and scorecards are batch work; their time is shared across tests and they are marked concurrent with the billing interface, because they do not hold the result or the billable order.
Rejected specimens and other cancellations reach this process through medical review as MRO-verified results.
Shares of copy problems, dilutes, queries, amendments, misdirected reports and billing exceptions are the author's estimates.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.35) except the added MRO assistant role.
